newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IPB RAISES KEY RATES FIVE PERCENTAGE PTS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH IPB RAISES KEY RATES FIVE PERCENTAGE PTS.

text.p: Prague based Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. , one of the four largest Czech banks, said that it would raise its key interest rates by five full percentage points beginning on Thursday.

In a statement, spokesman Jan Rezek said the bank's base rate for new credit would rise to 17.3 percent from 12.3 percent, and its rate for credits granted before the end of 1994 would rise to 21.3 percent from 16.3 percent.

The move joins rate hikes by other major Czech banks after the Czech National Bank pushed its last-resort Lombard credit rate to 50 percent from 14 percent last Friday, and its repo rate to 45 percent from 12.9 percent on Monday in an effort to stem a sharp drop in the Czech crown's exchange rate.

The Czech crown dropped to below five percent under parity with its mark/dollar basket last week as investors began to pull out of the currency amid poor macroeconomic results and and political instability.
